**Jeremy Gara** (born June 6, 1978) is a Canadian drummer from [Ottawa, Ontario](/wiki/Ottawa,_Ontario "Ottawa, Ontario"). He is most well known as the drummer of the band [Arcade Fire](/wiki/Arcade_Fire "Arcade Fire"). Gara is an active performer in a number of other projects, including work as a solo performer.[[1]](#cite_note-Never_Enough_Notes-1)

In March 2025[[97]](#cite_note-97), Google introduced an experimental "AI Mode" within its Search platform, enabling users to input complex, multi-part queries and receive comprehensive, AI-generated responses. This feature uses Google's advanced [Gemini](/wiki/Gemini_(chatbot) "Gemini (chatbot)") 2.0 model, which enhances the system's reasoning capabilities and supports multimodal inputs, including text, images, and voice.

Initially, AI Mode was available to [Google One](/wiki/Google_One "Google One") AI Premium subscribers in the United States, who could access it through the Search Labs platform. This phased rollout allowed Google to gather user feedback and refine the feature before a broader release.

Starting 9 March 2016, Lee played a five-game match, broadcast live, against the computer program [AlphaGo](/wiki/AlphaGo "AlphaGo"), developed by a London-based [artificial intelligence](/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") firm [Google DeepMind](/wiki/Google_DeepMind "Google DeepMind"), for a $1 million match prize.[[12]](#cite_note-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13)[[14]](#cite_note-14) He said “I have heard that Google DeepMind’s AI is surprisingly strong and getting stronger, but I am confident that I can win at least this time”.[[15]](#cite_note-15) In an interview with [Sohn Suk-hee](/wiki/Sohn_Suk-hee "Sohn Suk-hee") of [JTBC Newsroom](/wiki/JTBC_Newsroom "JTBC Newsroom") on 22 February 2016,[[16]](#cite_note-16) he showed confidence in his chances again, while saying that even beating AlphaGo by 4–1 may allow the Google DeepMind team to claim its *de facto* victory and the defeat of him, or even humanity. In this interview he pointed out [the time rule](/wiki/AlphaGo#Match_against_Lee_Sedol "AlphaGo") in this match, which seems well-balanced so that both he and the AI would fairly undergo time pressure. In another interview at Yonhap News, Lee Se-dol said that he was confident of beating AlphaGo by a score of 5–0, at least 4–1 and accepted the challenge in only five minutes. He also said "Of course, there would have been many updates in the last four or five months, but that isn’t enough time to challenge me".[[17]](#cite_note-17)

On 9 March, Lee played black and lost the first game by resignation.[[18]](#cite_note-18) On 10 March, he played white and lost the second game by resignation.[[19]](#cite_note-19) On 12 March, he played black and lost the third game as well.[[20]](#cite_note-20) On 13 March, he played white and won the fourth game, following an unexpected move at White 78 described as "a brilliant *[tesuji](/wiki/Tesuji "Tesuji")*", and by [Gu Li](/wiki/Gu_Li_(Go_player) "Gu Li (Go player)") 9 dan as a "[divine move](/wiki/Divine_move "Divine move")" and completely unforese

The Bordeaux [wine region](/wiki/Wine_region "Wine region") is divided into subregions including [Saint-Émilion](/wiki/Saint-%C3%89milion_AOC "Saint-Émilion AOC"), [Pomerol](/wiki/Pomerol_AOC "Pomerol AOC"), [Médoc](/wiki/M%C3%A9doc_AOC "Médoc AOC"), and [Graves](/wiki/Graves_(wine_region) "Graves (wine region)"). The 60 Bordeaux appellations and the wine styles they represent are usually categorized into six main families, four red based on the subregions and two white based on sweetness:[[18]](#cite_note-CIVB_prod-18)
* *Red Bordeaux and Red Bordeaux Supérieur*. Bordeaux winemakers may use the two regional appellations throughout the entire wine region; however, approximately half of the Bordeaux vineyard is specifically designated under Bordeaux and Bordeaux Supérieur [AOCs](/wiki/Appellation_d%27origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e "Appellation d'origine contrôlée"). With the majority of châteaux located on the Right Bank in the Entre-Deux-Mers area, wines are typically Merlot-dominant, often blended with the other classic Bordeaux varieties. There are many small, family-run châteaux, as well as wines blended and sold by wine merchants under commercial brand names. The Bordeaux AOC wines tend to be fruity, with minimal influence of [oak](/wiki/Oak_(wine) "Oak (wine)"), and are produced in a style meant to be drunk young. Bordeaux Superieur AOC wines are produced in the same area

As of May 2024, the brand was valued at US$2 billion.[[520]](#cite_note-time_rarebeauty-521)[[528]](#cite_note-529) In 2023, its estimated annual revenue reached US$300 million, up approximately 50 percent from 2022.[[529]](#cite_note-BOF_2024-530) The company was also included on *Time*'s list of the most influential companies of 2024.[[520]](#cite_note-time_rarebeauty-521) In September 2024, [Bloomberg L.P.](/wiki/Bloomberg_L.P. The Disney Channel airing of "[Phineas and Ferb Get Busted!](/wiki/Phineas_and_Ferb_Get_Busted! The Phoenix [Metropolitan Statistical Area](/wiki/Metropolitan_statistical_area "Metropolitan statistical area") (MSA) (officially known as the Phoenix-Mesa-Chandler MSA[[153]](#cite_note-155)), is one of 10 MSAs in Arizona, and was the 11th largest in the United States, with a 2018 U.S. census population estimate of 4,857,962, up from the 2010 census population of 4,192,887. Consisting of both Pinal and Maricopa counties, the MSA accounts for 65.5% of Arizona's population.[[150]](#cite_note-phoenix.about.com-152)[[151]](#cite_note-MSA-153) Phoenix only contributed 13% to the total growth rate of the MSA, down significantly from its 33% share during the prior decade.[[152]](#cite_note-Cox-154) Phoenix is also part of the [Arizona Sun Corridor](/wiki/Arizona_Sun_Corridor "Arizona Sun Corridor") [megaregion](/wiki/Megaregions_of_the_United_States "Megaregions of the United States") (MR), which is the tenth most populous of the 11 MRs, and the eighth largest by area. It had the second largest growth by percentage of the MRs (behind only the Gulf Coast MR) between 2000 and 2010.[[154]](#cite_note-156)

The population is almost equally split between men and women, with men making up 50.2% of city's citizens. The population density is 2,797.8 people per square mile, and the city's median age is 32.2 years, with only 10.9 of the population being over 62. 98.5% of Phoenix's population lives in households with an average household size of 2.77 people.

There were 514,806 total households, with 64.2% of those households consisting of families: 42.3% married couples, 7% with an unmarried male as head of household, and 14.9% with an unmarried female as head of household. 33.6% of those households have children below the age of 18. Of the 35.8% of non-family households, 27.1% have a householder living alone, almost evenly split between men and women, with women having 13.7% and men occupying 13.5%.

In 2009, around 40 percent of Parisians held a *[licence](/wiki/Licence_(France) "Licence (France)")*-level diploma or higher, the highest proportion in France.[[330]](#cite_note-332) 13 percent have no diploma, the third-lowest percentage in France. Education in Paris and the Île-de-France region employs approximately 330,000 people, 170,000 of whom are teachers and professors, teaching approximately 2.9 million students in around 9,000 primary, secondary, and higher education schools and institutions.[[331]](#cite_note-idf_education-333)

The [University of Paris](/wiki/University_of_Paris "University of Paris"), founded in the 12th century, is often called the [Sorbonne](/wiki/University_of_Paris "University of Paris") after one of its original medieval colleges. In 1970, it was broken up into [thirteen autonomous universities](/wiki/List_of_universities_and_institutions_in_the_Paris_region "List of universities and institutions in the Paris region") following the [student demonstrations in 1968](/wiki/May_68 "May 68"). Most of the campuses today are in the [Latin Quarter](/wiki/Latin_Quarter,_Paris "Latin Quarter, Paris"), where the old university was located, while others are scattered around the city and the suburbs.[[332]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECombeau2013213–214-334)

The Paris region hosts France's highest concentration of the *[grandes écoles](/wiki/Grandes_%C3%A9coles "Grandes écoles")* – 55 specialised centres of higher education outside or inside the public university structure. 2022 NBA Finals :: Redesigned logo and trophy :: chunk_0019
On April 13, the NBA released a reimagined version of the classic NBA Finals wordmark that was used between 1986 and 1995 and from 2004 to 2017. The new logo also features a depiction of the [Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy](/wiki/Larry_O%27Brien_Championship_Trophy "Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy") in the background.[[71]](#cite_note-71)

The NBA then announced on May 12 that the Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy and the [Bill Russell NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Trophy](/wiki/NBA_Finals_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award") have also been redesigned. Among the new changes to the Larry O'Brien Trophy, its base now consists of two disks that list the names of all the previous winning teams. The Bill Russell Trophy has been changed from a gold ball and silver net to primarily gold with silver accents.[[72]](#cite_note-72)

Russell died at his Mercer Island, Washington, home on July 31, 2022, at the age of 88.[[73]](#cite_note-Goldstein_2022-73)[[74]](#cite_note-74) The news was announced in a [Twitter post](/wiki/Twitter_post "Twitter post") by his family. In a statement, NBA Commissioner [Adam Silver](/wiki/Adam_Silver "Adam Silver") said that Russell was "the greatest champion in all of team sports".[[75]](#cite_note-75)

With NBA commissioner [Adam Silver](/wiki/Adam_Silver "Adam Silver") missing games 5 and 6 due to the league's health and safety protocols, the Larry O'Brien Trophy was presented to the Warriors by deputy commissioner [Mark Tatum](/wiki/Mark_Tatum "Mark Tatum") instead.[[76]](#cite_note-76)

Levels of income inequality in Honduras are higher than in any other Latin American country.[[94]](#cite_note-elcorreo.eu.org-98) Unlike other Latin American countries, inequality steadily increased in Honduras between 1991 and 2005.[[99]](#cite_note-econstor.eu-103) Between 2006 and 2010 inequality saw a decrease but increased again in 2010.[[94]](#cite_note-elcorreo.eu.org-98)

When Honduras's [Human Development Index](/wiki/Human_Development_Index "Human Development Index") is adjusted for inequality (known as the IHDI) Honduras's development index is reduced to .443.[[10]](#cite_note-:1-14) The levels of inequality in each aspect of development can also be assessed.[[10]](#cite_note-:1-14) In 2015 inequality of life expectancy at birth was 19.6%, inequality in education was 24.4% and inequality in income was 41.5% [[10]](#cite_note-:1-14) The overall loss in human development due to inequality was 29.2.[[10]](#cite_note-:1-14)

The IHDI for Latin America and the Caribbean overall is 0.575 with an overall loss of 23.4%.[[10]](#cite_note-:1-14) In 2015 for the entire region, inequality of life expectancy at birth was 22.9%, inequality in education was 14.0% and inequality in income was 34.9%.[[10]](#cite_note-:1-14) While Honduras has a higher life expectancy than other countries in the region (before and after inequality adjustments), its quality of education and economic standard of living are lower.[[10]](#cite_note-:1-14) Income inequality and education inequality have a large impact on the overall development of the nation.[[10]](#cite_note-:1-14)

Inequality also exists between rural and urban areas as it relates to the distribution of resources.[[102]](#cite_note-106) Poverty is concentrated in southern, eastern, and western regions where rural and indigenous peoples live.
